A CTA night, start to finish

Nine steps. The officer is needed for four of them: starting the signup, logging the CTA once, choosing where attendance comes from and closing the signup. With the automatic split on, everything after logging is the bot's. The setting is chosen once, in the guild's setup.

  1. Post the signup/cta start with a tab of your sheet and a start time.🔒 Officer
  2. Members sign upA drop-down on the post. The roster and your sheet update as they click.🟢 Any member
  3. Reminders go outEveryone who signed up is pinged before the start. The server event is already on the Events list.🤖 The bot does this
  4. The whole timer is collectedThe bot watches Albion's battle list for the entire timer, keeps one post for it up to date and keeps looking for fights Albion lists late.🤖 The bot does this
  5. Log the CTAIn the signup thread press Log this CTA, post the screenshots, check the preview, press Log it. It is the officer's last job on the split.🔒 Officer
  6. Attendance comes from your choiceThe signup spreadsheet, the battleboard fights, or both. Both takes everyone on either list, so nobody is missed.🔒 Officer
  7. The bot finishes the splitIf your guild chose it: the bot reads the timer's battleboards, adds everyone who was there (registering anyone who isn't by matching their Discord name), leaves out other content at the same time such as three people ratting, and waits until no new battleboard has turned up for 6 hours. Otherwise an officer checks the split and pays it as before. See it🤖 The bot does this
  8. Everyone is told twicePing 1: each person's share, credited to their balance. Ping 2: once the loot thread is finished, what was added and their combined total. A battleboard listed late credits only the people it adds.🤖 The bot does this
  9. Close the signupClose signups takes the event off the Events list, clears the sheet's sign-up column and posts the recap with the no-shows.🔒 Officer
Meanwhile, without anyone doing anything. The bot finds deaths on the killboard for regear requests and keeps checking until they appear, checks for loot that never reached the chest, keeps the battleboard post up to date, registers members whose Discord name is their character's name, tidies nicknames and tags at night, posts the weekly summary and takes a backup every night.
Extra, only if loot goes missing. /lootcheck lists loot that never reached the chest and opens a thread with a card for each player. When a player hands loot back, the officer presses Resolved and picks Loot returned: the bot adds it to that night's split as late loot, and everyone's share for that CTA goes up by itself. Nothing is logged again. A chest log posted later in the thread settles cards the same way, counting only deposits made within 48 hours of the fight.

CTA signups & builds

Signing up for a CTA

A CTA signup is one post. The roles come from a tab of your Google Sheet, one numbered row per role. Members claim a role from a drop-down, the bot keeps the roster up to date, and every pick is written back to the sheet.

1Start it with one command

🎟️ Starter role or officer

Choose the composition tab of your sheet, give it a title and a start time (UTC, Albion's clock). The time also creates the server event and sets the reminders.

2Members pick a role

🟢 Any member

The post shows the roster as a table: every role, who has it and what is still open. Members choose a role from the drop-down, where each choice starts with its weapon's icon. Tentative ("I might come", never counted as a no-show), Bomb and Fill are buttons, Builds shows the gear for each role, and Leave or Withdraw takes them off.

3Members get their build

🟢 Any member

Claiming a role answers with its build, privately. The pictures are the game's own: a grid of the gear, a small +1 where a slot has another choice that is just as good, a number where you bring more than one, and under it the skills and passives for each piece. Below the picture is the same list as text. Another build… opens any of the comp's other builds and Send me this in DMs sends it to your messages. The builds come from a builds tab in your Google Sheet, where every cell is a drop-down: the items, the tiers and the skills each piece can really have (a plate chest such as Guardian Armor lists its three actives and its passives).

4The thread and the reminder

🤖 The bot does this

Each section of the composition gets its own card in the signup's thread, with who has claimed what. Before the start the bot reminds everyone who signed up and names the roles still open.

5After the CTA

🤖 The bot does this

When the loot is logged the bot posts a recap: who signed up and showed, who didn't, and who came without signing up.

The roster table is a picture the bot draws, so the colours always match the roles.

CTA lootsplit & loot check

Splitting the loot and checking the chest

After the fight an officer posts the screenshots and the bot does the sums. A loot check then shows who took loot and never put it in the chest. Paying members out is a separate job that happens outside the night.

1Post the screenshots

🔒 Officer

The guild bank tab, the repair window and the party list. A battle link works too, and then the attendance comes from the battle.

2Log a CTA and read the screenshots

🔒 Officer

Log a CTA in the officer menu asks for a name, the loot and the repair. 📷 Read screenshots then reads the pictures and shows what it found: the loot value, the repair cost and the people in the party list. Names it only half matched are listed so you can check them.

3Check the preview, then Log it

🔒 Officer

The preview is the whole split: tax, the guild's cut and each player's share (1,930,714 each for 14 people here). Nothing is saved until you press Log it.

4Choose where the attendance comes from

🔒 Officer

Under the preview, After Log it, add attendees from… is your choice: the signup spreadsheet, the battleboard fights, or both. Both takes everyone on either list, so nobody is missed. Only people in both lists is stricter and Nobody yet leaves it for later. After Log it the bot shows who it found and waits for Add These To The Event. Pressing Log this CTA in the signup thread opens this same form with the event's name filled in.

5The loot card

🤖 The bot does this

The card in your loot channel lists every share, and each share goes onto the member's balance. Edit this split fixes a mistake and everyone's share is recalculated. Paying a balance out is a separate job (see Member payouts); Mark shares paid is there for a guild that pays on the night.

6Who didn't deposit?

🔒 Officer

/lootcheck compares the Loot Logger export with the guild chest log. What someone died carrying is shown separately and isn't blamed on them. A loot thread can then chase the rest.

7Following up in the thread

🔒 Officer

A loot thread gives each player who still owes loot a card with Retry deathlog search and Resolved. The header counts what is open, and its buttons search again, check a newer chest log, ping the players or close the thread.

8Extra: when a player hands the loot back

🔒 Officer

This is only for loot that went missing, and it isn't part of the night's steps. On the player's card press Resolved and pick Loot returned. The bot finds that night's split and shows the total and every share before and after. Add to the split and resolve puts the loot in as late loot: the total goes up and everyone's share for that CTA, and so their balance, is worked out again by itself. The other choices (died carrying it, traded, gave back their own gear) settle the card without adding silver.

9Later evidence: the fights' kill lists and a newer chest log

🔒 Officer

Two things can settle a card after the thread is open. Retry deathlog search also reads the kill lists of the night's battleboard fights, which are complete before a player's own killboard page shows the death. And after somebody deposits late, post a newer chest log in the thread and press 🧾 Check a newer chest log. The bot shows what it would settle and changes nothing until you choose. Only deposits made after the thread opened and within 48 hours of the fight count, so the same item deposited after a different CTA is never mistaken for this one's loot. A late deposit of loot somebody still owes is listed as a warning, and that card stays open for you to settle by hand. A card it settles adds its silver to the CTA's split as late loot, and Reopen takes it back out.

10Closing a thread

🔒 Officer

Close thread asks first. Closing stops the reminders, marks the header closed and archives the thread. Nothing is deleted or paid, the cards stay readable, and Reopen thread brings it back.

The loot check's "Worth knowing" notes mention the killboard because this example has no real killboard behind it.

Automatic split

A CTA's split that finishes itself

In a guild that chose The bot finishes it by itself, the officer logs the split once and the bot does the rest: it adds who was there, waits for late fights, credits every share to the member's balance and tells each person twice. The choice is made in the guild's setup, and an officer can step in at any point.

1The bot takes it from here

🔒 Officer 🤖 The bot does this

After the officer logs the split, the signup thread gets one status message. It lists the fights the bot counted, the fights it left out and why, how many people are on the split and what it is waiting for. Three people ratting somewhere else at the same time are not on the CTA's split. A fight whose people were also in the CTA's fights counts even if it is small, because you only appear on a battleboard when you die or your party gets a kill. A fight the bot can't place is listed, and if it is worth a look an officer is asked once.

2Ping 1: everybody's share

🤖 The bot does this

Nobody is told anything until the timer is over and no new battleboard has turned up for 6 hours (a setting, 1 to 24). Then every share is credited to the member's balance and each person gets one ping with their share.

3A late fight pings only the new people

🤖 The bot does this

Albion can list a fight hours late. The people it adds are credited right away and pinged on their own. Everyone who was already credited keeps what they were credited and is not pinged again.

4Ping 2: what was added

🤖 The bot does this

When the loot thread is finished, and every question about a fight has an answer, everybody whose total grew is told what was added and their combined total for the CTA. That is two pings for each person, never more.

5What the officers can do

🔒 Officer

The status message has the buttons: Send pings now skips the waiting, Hold pings stops them until Release the hold, Include a fight adds a fight the bot left out, Different timer points it at another timer and Undo the credits takes every credit back out of the balances. Switch to manual hands the split to an officer. If something stops the bot from finishing within a day of the timer, it hands the split over and pings nobody.

These screens come from the test menu's pretend CTA night: Albion's fights and the people in them are made up.

Combined battleboard

Fight summaries without the links

The battleboard watches Albion's battle list for your guild, so nobody pastes links. For a CTA it keeps one post for the whole timer: it collects every fight of that timer, including fights Albion lists hours late, and edits the post as they arrive. Your guild can choose to have each fight posted on its own, the whole timer in one post, or both.

1The timer's fights are collected in one post

🤖 The bot does this

A timer is a two-hour window around the game-time hour, so the 02 UTC timer covers 01:30 to 03:29. The bot posts one breakdown when it finds the timer's first fight, edits it as more fights are listed, and keeps looking for three days because Albion can be slow to list a fight. The post has the totals on both sides and pages to flip through: Composition shows who brought what, Kill timeline the order of the kills, Momentum which side was winning and when. When the night is over an officer logs the CTA from the signup thread, and can add the attendance from these fights. If your guild has set up regear requests, each post also carries a File a regear button. A guild on the Loot split only style never gets it.

2The tempo of the fight

🤖 The bot does this

Kill timeline shows how the fight went: who was killing and when. Momentum shows the swing. Together they show whether you lost the fight early or kept losing it for ten minutes.

3Who brought what

🤖 The bot does this

The composition page counts the weapons on each side. With a Builds tab in your sheet the bot also tells your own roles apart.

4Who is winning your fights

🟢 Any member

/leaderboard ranks your players over the fights the battleboard has counted: Kills, K/D, (K+A)/D and Most deaths, for 7 days, 30 days or all time. Only the member sees it. Ten players show at a time. A longer board has Prev and Next, Find me (jumps to the page with one of your characters and points an arrow at your row) and Find a name. Officers also get Post here to put the page they are looking at in the channel.

The fights and the players are made up. The pictures are the ones the bot draws.

Officer menus & setup

What officers see

Officers work from one menu, /officer, and one list, /inbox. The first-time setup is a short checklist that the bot walks through with you.

1First-time setup

🔒 Officer

/help opens a checklist with a bar showing how far you are. Each page says what to do next and takes you to the right setting. You can leave and come back.

2The settings menu

🔒 Officer

Every setting is in one menu, grouped by what it does. The bot says where each one lives, so "turn this on in the settings menu" is never a puzzle.

3The officer menu

🔒 Officer

One menu for the jobs officers do most: log a CTA, look up a member, pay what is owed, upload the Siphoned Energy log. Anything that moves money asks first.

4Everything waiting on you

🔒 Officer

/inbox lists regears to approve, shares to pay and anything else that needs an officer, most pressing first. It only shows and links. Nothing happens until you press a button.

Automated regears

Regears without the spreadsheet

Regears are in silver. A member files a request, the bot finds the death and prices the gear, and an officer approves. The silver goes onto the member's balance, so nobody has to send anything first.

Silver regears only. The bot doesn't regear physical items. If your guild does, ask Birdman on Discord (thebirdman_94).

1A member files a request

🟢 Any member

File a regear opens a private thread. The member says what happened and can add a screenshot.

2The bot finds the death

🤖 The bot does this

It looks for the death on the killboard. If the killboard hasn't published it yet, the request waits: the bot looks again after a day, then daily for a week, and pings when it turns up. Check now looks straight away.

3The ticket

🤖 The bot does this

The ticket shows the death, the gear that was lost, whether the player was on a CTA, and what they have had in regears lately. Officers get the ping.

4Approve onto the balance

🔒 Officer

Approve & pay to wallet asks once, and says plainly that no silver is sent in the game. The amount goes onto the member's balance. If your officers would rather pay in the game straight away, Approve at guild rate and mark it paid afterwards. Both are in the same menu.

5The member sees it

🟢 Any member

/balance shows what is owed, including approved regears. It is paid out later with the rest, when it suits both sides.

The balance screens are in Member payouts.

Siphoned energy

Siphoned Energy without the spreadsheet

Siphoned Energy is tracked from the game's own log. Upload it, and the bot shows every member's balance and who is behind.

1Upload the log

🔒 Officer

/siphon upload reads the file, counts only the lines it hasn't seen, and shows who is behind. Undo this upload removes just the lines that upload added.

2The report and one member

🔒 Officer

The report lists everyone. A member's page lists what they put in and took out.

3Ping the members who are behind

🔒 Officer

The ping is previewed first, with the names it will mention. Then it is posted.

4The reminder to upload again

🤖 The bot does this

When it has been a while, the bot asks the officers to upload again.

Audits

Audits and who has left

A nightly audit compares your Discord with Albion's guild list. It reports who left, registers who it can, and asks the rest to /register. Nobody loses a role until an officer confirms.

1The nightly report

🤖 The bot does this

What the audit did tonight: who it registered by name, which names it looked up, who it asked to /register, and anything it couldn't do and why.

2Asking an officer first

🔒 Officer

Removing a role is never automatic. The bot lists who it would change and waits.

Member payouts

What members are owed and how it is paid

Members always know what they are owed, and officers pay it out whenever it suits. The bot never sends silver in the game. It keeps the balance, and an officer records each payment.

1A member checks

🟢 Any member

/balance shows what is owed, split into loot, regears and credits. /balances history lists where it came from. /me is the member's page.

2The bot tells them

🤖 The bot does this

Members owed silver get a weekly message, and the officers get a weekly summary.

3An officer pays out

🔒 Officer

/pay, or Pay what's owed in the member menu, pays out the member's whole balance: everything is marked paid and the balance goes to zero. The bot only records it; it never sends silver itself.

Newcomer registration

From newcomer to member

A newcomer is welcomed, types their character name once, and the bot checks it with Albion and gives them the right role and nickname.

1The welcome

🤖 The bot does this

A short message points them to where they apply and to /register.

2They register

🟢 Any member

/register checks the character with Albion, gives the role, sets the nickname and updates the sheets.

Builds

Builds: the gear each role brings

A build is the gear one role brings: every piece with its picture, tier and amount, the choices that are just as good, and the skills and passives. The builds live on one tab of your Google Sheet, the BUILDS tab, and the bot reads them from there each time. Members look at them in Discord. Officers make and change them in Discord or in the sheet itself.

Every screen here is the bot's own. The sheet is drawn from the cells the bot really wrote.

1Look at a build

🟢 Any member

/builds show lists the builds to pick from. Give it a name (build:) and it opens that one straight away. The window is private. It shows the gear as the game's own picture, then the same list as text. Under each piece are its skills and passives. Another build… switches to any other, and Send me this in DMs keeps a copy.

2Put a comp's builds in front of everyone

🔒 Officer

/builds post posts a comp (a CTA tab of your sheet) in the builds channel. Every role is listed with the build it brings, and members pick theirs from the menu. A build is read from the sheet when it is opened, so the post is never out of date. You are told how many roles have no build yet, and which.

3Send a build to one person

🔒 Officer

/builds send puts a build in a member's DMs, with your name on it. If their privacy settings block it, the bot says so and gives them the command to open it themselves.

4Make a build without leaving Discord

🎟️ Starter role or officer

/builds create opens a private editor. Pick a slot, type an item's name (a misspelling gets a "Did you mean…" list), set the tier and enchantment, and the picture of the gear is drawn as you go. Each slot can have up to three choices. Skills… lists only what that piece can really have: Q, W, E, an active and a passive. Nothing is on the sheet until you press Save to the sheet.

5Change or remove one

🎟️ Starter role or officer

/builds edit opens a build you already have in the same editor. Only the cells that differ are written, so nothing else on the sheet is touched. /builds delete asks first and empties the build's cells; your formatting stays.

6The same builds on the sheet

🔒 Officer

The BUILDS tab is a table: one row for each piece, one colour for each build, and a drop-down in every cell. The item cell offers the items of its slot. The Q, W, E, SKILL, PASSIVE and PASSIVE 2 cells offer the skills that piece can really have (you can type to search). A spelling a list doesn't have is allowed, and marked. A plate armour has two passives, each from its own list: PASSIVE offers Toughness, Authority, Tenacity, and PASSIVE 2 offers Spirit Crush or Protective Instinct. Every other piece has one passive, so its PASSIVE 2 cell stays empty. A cape has nothing to choose, only its item and tier.

7First-time setup

🔒 Officer

/builds setup shows two looks side by side with made-up examples, so you can choose: the original table pictures, or builds. Use builds, table sheet makes the BUILDS tab. Draft from my comps then reads the weapons, helm, armor and boots you wrote on your comp tabs and shows what it would make. Rows that name no tier need one picked. A tier is never invented, and nothing is written until you press Write.

8Where things stand

🔒 Officer

/builds status is the checklist: the sheet, the tab, how many builds, and for each comp how many roles have one. Its buttons sync from comps, make a build, give a role its build, choose the look and recolour the roles. Refresh drop-downs rewrites the lists and puts the drop-downs back on every row after the game adds items, or when someone pasted over them. It changes nothing you typed. Skill lists can make the skill drop-downs follow the item on their row; it is marked a trial and can be turned off again.

The sheet is the database. Whatever the editor writes is the layout an officer can also type or pick by hand.

Offtimers

Offtimers: side content apart from the CTA

An offtimer is a small roam or side content that runs apart from the CTA. It has its own signup, its own sheet tabs and its own list of events, and its loot is shared the same way: the guild's cut first, then an equal share to everyone who came. The silver lands in each member's balance. It is never sent in the game.

Every screen here is the bot's own, captured from the offtimer commands, run with example players.

1Start a signup

🎟️ Starter role or officer

/offtimer start takes a tab from the Offtimer sheet tabs list (a CTA tab is refused) and posts the ping with a thread. It works like a CTA: a role from the Pick your role drop-down, or type its number in the thread, and Tentative, Bomb, Leave, Withdraw and the two Fill buttons. The roster under the post updates as people claim. The officer is told where it started.

2Claim or free a role for someone

🎟️ Starter role or officer

/offtimer claimfor claims a role for a member who can't, or frees one and names who held it. A release can't name a member: it frees whoever holds that number.

3Close the signup

🎟️ Starter role or officer

/offtimer close is run inside the thread. No more claims are taken, the roles stay as they were, and the comp sheet's sign-up column is cleared for the next one. Typing a number afterwards does nothing.

4Turn the thread into a payout

🔒 Officer

/offtimer import is run inside the thread. Everyone who claimed a role, or is on the fill or bomb list, is an attendee. The bot takes the tax rate and repairs, pays each attendee's balance, closes the thread and clears the sign-up column. It needs the loot, and refuses the numbers that can't be right.

5Someone came late

🔒 Officer

Run it again with additional_players and the bot shows what changes for everyone before it does anything: the new share, who is added and who is lowered. Apply Recalculated Split pays the latecomer and lowers the others to the new equal share. Run again with no one to add, it says the thread was already imported.

6Only count who came

🔒 Officer

With reporting_only:True there is no loot: the bot records who attended, and no balance changes. The record counts for activity and attendance, and it stays apart from the CTA events.

7Log one without a thread

🔒 Officer

/offtimer log is for an offtimer that had no signup thread: a name, the loot, who came, and the repair cost and tax rate if they differ. The attendees' balances are credited at once, and a payout notice names each of them. Leave out the name, the loot or the players and a short form opens instead, with a member picker and a preview before anything is paid.

8Look an event up

🔒 Officer

/offtimer info with an event number shows its whole breakdown: the loot, the repairs, the guild's cut and what each attendee was paid. With no number it lists the recent events (limit: says how many). An offtimer never counts in /balances fund's break-even rate.

9Take someone off, or delete the event

🔒 Officer

/offtimer unattend removes players and shares the loot between the rest. The preview says whose credit is taken back and who gets more, and nothing changes until Apply Recalculated Split is pressed. /offtimer delete asks the same way and reverses every attendee's balance for the event.

An offtimer's loot never touches a CTA's numbers, and its events have their own list.

CTA tools

Looking after a CTA once it is posted

The commands that look after a CTA once it is posted. A caller with the CTA starter role can run the first three; the others are for officers. Every screen is the bot's own, from the commands run with example players.

1Claim or free a role for someone

🎟️ Starter role or officer

/cta claimfor claims a role number for a member, or releases it. Claiming a second role for someone frees their first one, and says so. Releasing a role nobody holds, or running it outside the thread, says what is wrong instead of guessing.

2Close the signup

🎟️ Starter role or officer

/cta close is run inside the thread. No more claims are taken, the event is taken off the server's Events list, and the comp sheet's sign-up column is cleared. Tie it to a logged event with event_id: and the bot works out the no-show list and a recap. Running it again says it is already closed.

3Who may start and close CTAs

🔒 Officer

/cta starter-role shows the role that may run /cta start, /cta close and /cta claimfor here, sets one, or clears it. Without one, only full officers can. Offtimers have their own starter role in the settings menu.

4Change a post after it is out

🎟️ Starter role or officer

/signup-edit is run inside the signup thread. It can change the title (the post, the thread's name and the server event change with it), move or remove the start time, add or remove a note line, and pick the board, the roster look under the post. Nobody is pinged by an edit. A time it can't read changes nothing. The composition and the claims are left alone.

5Watch for the fights of a timer

🔒 Officer

/cta battlewatch looks at the guild's recent fights every 30 minutes over a time range you give, and pings you when fights turn up that have enough players, and enough of yours, so other people's fights are skipped. A timer is often more than one fight and Albion can list one hours late, so it keeps looking for a few days. It adds nobody to an event by itself: Review & add attendees opens the list of fights to tick.

The signup and the loot split themselves are in the chapters before this one.

Roster & giveaways

Who is in the guild, and giving silver to the top players

The roster is who is in the guild: who they are, which kit they play, who recruited them and who is away. A giveaway pays silver to the top players of a period. All of it is for officers, and everything that moves silver or removes someone shows a preview first. The screens are the bot's own, with example players.

1Keep the roster

🔒 Officer

/roster add puts a player on the roster (or updates them) with the kit role they play, /roster remove takes them off and /roster list shows everyone.

2Time off and exemptions

🔒 Officer

/roster timeoff keeps a member out of /roster inactivity until a date. /roster auditexempt does the same for /registration audit. A date it can't read (next week) is refused and nothing is saved.

3Recruits and their reward

🔒 Officer

/roster recruits action:record notes who recruited a player. When the recruit reaches the number of CTAs the guild chose, the recruiter is credited, right away if they already have them. action:show lists a recruiter's recruits and how far each one is.

4Who is still in the game roster

🔒 Officer

/roster kickcheck takes the guild's in-game roster export and checks it against the bot's registration records: who still holds the guild role, who has left Discord but not the game guild, and who was never registered. It never assumes anyone needs kicking just because the bot doesn't know them.

5Give silver to the top players

🔒 Officer

/giveaway run ranks the players of a period by CTA attendance, or by PvE fame, and shows who would win and what each gets before anyone is credited. Ties at the cutoff all win. Only the officer who ran it can confirm, and a second press does nothing. Each winner's balance is credited and a payout notice names them.

Role handouts (/role bulk, role panels) are in the chapter that follows.

Roles

Handing out roles

Handing out roles to many people at once, and letting members take their own. /role bulk and /role copy need the Discord Manage Roles permission. Role panels and the strip-roles list are for officers. The bot never gives a role it can't manage, and it says why.

1Give or take a role for a list of people

🔒 Officer

/role bulk adds or removes a role for everyone you @mention or paste as user IDs. The answer sorts them: done, already had it, not found, or failed (and why). A role above the bot's own, a managed role, @everyone, or a list with nobody in it is refused with the reason.

2Copy a role to everyone who holds others

🔒 Officer

/role copy gives one role to everyone who holds any of up to three other roles. The preview counts who would get it and who has it already, and nothing happens until Grant to everyone shown. Only whoever ran the command can press it.

3A panel where members take their own role

🔒 Officer

/reactionroles create posts a panel: members click an emoji to get a role and click again to drop it. You pick the roles from a list and see a preview first. A role with powerful permissions (Administrator, Manage Roles) is left out: it has to be handed out by an officer. The bot needs to add reactions in the channel, and says so if it can't.

4Change a panel

🔒 Officer

/reactionroles edit adds or removes a role (with the emoji you choose, or the next number), turns Pick one only on or off, or deletes the panel. Taking a role off the panel doesn't take it from anyone who has it: /role bulk does. /reactionroles list shows the panels with a link to each.

5Roles the registration audit also takes away

🔒 Officer

/registration audit removes the Guild or Ally role of someone it confirms has left. /settings striproles adds more roles to take away at the same time (a recruiter role, a squad lead role), lists them and removes them again.

Tracking

Fame, fights, early leavers and objectives

What the bot keeps an eye on between events: members' fame, the guild's fights, who leaves a CTA early, and the open-world objectives. Most of it is for officers. Everything here is the bot's own screens, with example players.

1Fame: a member's numbers and the weekly report

🔒 Officer

/fame check reads a member's PvP and PvE fame from Albion, using their verified character (or any name you type). /fame report takes the weekly snapshot and says who is up and who is down since the last one; members who are on time off, or new, are listed apart. It also runs by itself every week.

2Fame: who is no longer in the guild

🔒 Officer

/fame audit checks everyone being tracked against Albion and shows who is no longer in the guild or its alliance. A member it couldn't check is left alone and not flagged. Stop Tracking Everyone Flagged takes them off, and only the officer who ran it can press it.

3Battleboard: the settings

🔒 Officer

/battleboard config chooses which guild or alliance to follow, the channel, how often to look, and how big a fight has to be to be posted. Run it with only the option you want to change. /battleboard status shows the whole picture, and /battleboard test makes a check right now. /battleboard stop turns the posting off.

4Who leaves CTAs early

🔒 Officer

A member who leaves early three times in a week sets off a card in the channel you pick. It says only that someone reached the limit: the name is behind Show who, and only officers can press it. An officer sees how many times it was counted, can excuse one, and /battleboard leftearly shows the history for 7 days, 30 days or all time.

5Open-world objectives

🟢 Any member

The objectives board lists dragons, chests and the rest, soonest first, with a live countdown. Anyone can press Report an objective to add one. The report asks what kind it is and says what it put on the board, with Undo. Officers can take one off with /objectives remove, and /objectives status says what the board and the optional scanner are doing.

Regear commands

Regears and balances, step by step

The regear screens the officers use every day, and the button members press. Nothing is paid until an officer presses a button, and every payment is a balance credit and a payout notice. The screens are the bot's own, with example players.

1Find a death and regear the kit

🔒 Officer

/regear kit looks a member's recent deaths up on the killboard (type their in-game name, or pick the member if they registered). The kit is listed with its prices: tick the items to regear, then choose the guild rate, a custom percentage or a fixed amount. An item with no price is flagged, and Set missing prices asks for it. Only the officer who opened the kit can use its buttons. A death already filed is named, not paid twice.

2No death yet, or several

🔒 Officer

The killboard can lag the game by hours. With no death in 7 days the bot offers Watch for a new death: it checks every 30 minutes and pings you here when one shows up. With several deaths it asks which one, and marks the ones already claimed.

3File a regear by hand, and look claims up

🔒 Officer

/regear claim files a claim with a reason and a fixed amount, for something the kit screen doesn't cover (a mount lost to a gank). A claim linked to an event needs the member to be confirmed on it. /regear info lists the claims by status, or opens one claim by its number.

4The File a regear button

🔒 Officer 🟢 Any member

/regear panel posts a File a regear button in a channel. A member presses it after a death: the bot finds the death on the killboard and opens a thread with what the officers need. The settings choose the channel, whether the threads are public or private, and which roles are regear officers.

5Give silver to another member

🟢 Any member

/balances give gives some of your own balance to another member (if the officers switched it on). A private window shows both balances before and after, and nothing moves until Give it. The notice in the payments channel carries the reason. Giving more than you have, or giving it to yourself, is refused and says why.

Game lookups

Lookups for the game itself

Five lookups that need nothing set up: /disarray, /route, /mastery show, /price and /alt list. The answers are private unless the person asks to post them (share:True on /disarray). The screens are the bot's own, with example players, and the numbers come from the game's wiki and market, as the bot read them.

1Disarray: what a group size costs

🟢 Any member

/disarray turns a group's size into its Disarray level. The level you have against the one you meet decides it: a lower level loses that many percent of damage and crowd-control time, and an equal or higher one loses nothing. Give players:150, add mounts:4 chariot, 2 rhino, 1 eagle for the battle mounts (points above 15 add a level each), level:46 for the group a level takes, or enemy: to compare two groups. A word that could mean two mounts is asked about and not guessed. With nothing typed it lists every level.

2Route: the way between two zones

🟢 Any member

/route takes two zones (start typing and pick from the list) and draws the shortest way: every zone in order with its colour and tier, how far it is in zone widths, and which city's portal it takes. Swap ends turns it round, and Avoid red zones or Avoid black zones looks for another way, or says there is none and shows the plain one.

3Mastery: what you have played

🟢 Any member

Playing a weapon or battle mount in the guild's CTAs and offtimers earns it levels. /mastery show is your page: tabs for all, weapons and mounts, the ones closest to their next level, and a search. Only the person who opened a page can press its buttons. An officer can add plays by hand, and the answer says the level it is now. A class that is no weapon is refused, not guessed.

4Price: the market for an item

🟢 Any member

/price takes an item as you type it: a game id, or plain words like 7.3 rift glaive or t8 beef stew. Food and resources work too. It shows where it is cheapest to buy, the best buy order to sell into and your home city's price, with how old each is. An item nobody lists is explained.

5Alts: more than one character

🟢 Any member

/alt list shows your main character and your alts, and /alt add links another character after checking it with the game. In a signup thread you then type the role number and the character: 5 AldricAlt. Battle and sheet attendance counts it for you.

These lookups change nothing on the server, except an officer adding mastery plays and a member linking an alt.

Setup & settings

Setting the bot up

A new server starts with /help. It opens a checklist that walks an officer through the first hour: what to set, in what order, and what each thing does. Every setting is then in one menu. Only officers can press any of it, and nothing saves until you choose it.

1Pick how the guides look

🔒 Officer

The first time, the bot asks how its guides should look: plain text, plain text with large headings, or boxes. Discord draws text inside a box smaller than ordinary chat text and a bot can't choose a size, so these are the three looks it can give. Change the look on the first page changes it again.

2Do the next thing

🔒 Officer

Next thing to do opens the first step that still needs doing, with the control for it on the page. Picking a channel posts the settings menu there and ticks the step. No typing and no other menu.

3Choose your officer role

🔒 Officer

Until you do, only people with the Manage Server permission count as officers. Pick the role and it saves at once. @everyone is refused, because it would give every member officer access, and nothing changes.

4Look over everything before you start

🔒 Officer

The last step pages through every part of the settings menu with what is set now. Anything that is on but can't work yet is listed under Needs attention.

5The settings menu

🔒 Officer

One button for each of the sixteen parts of the bot, then See everything. A part's page shows its settings under headings. Change a setting… opens one, and Go to another category… moves on. See everything lists what is on or missing and Fix them one by one takes you through them.

6Switch off what you don't use

🔒 Officer

Functions turns whole parts of the bot off for this server. An off function's commands leave the / list and /help, and its buttons go. Nothing is deleted: switch it on and everything is back. A member who still reaches it is told it is off and where an officer turns it on.

7Check on the bot

🔒 Officer

/server-status is private. It shows the build that is running, how long it has been up, how fast Discord answers, the servers it serves, and every background job: a tick for a healthy one, a cross for a job that crashed, a warning for one that isn't loaded.

8Welcome newcomers

🔒 Officer 🤖 The bot does this

/welcome sets the message the bot posts when someone joins: where it goes (a channel or a private message), where to apply, and your own wording if you want it. The default points to where they apply and to /register.

9Start a new guild from a copy of your sheet

🔒 Officer

/settings cleansheet empties a copy of your sheet and leaves your live one alone: the comp tabs, layout and formulas stay and the people go. It shows what it will empty first and nothing happens until you press the button.

Registration

Registering people

Members register themselves with /register. These are the officer's side of it: registering someone who can't, fixing what went wrong, writing the guide people read, and the settings. Officers of a server that only has registration (a register-only server) can use the same commands there.

1Register someone else

🔒 Officer

/registration other does what /register does, run for the member. It checks the character with Albion, gives the guild or ally role, sets the nickname, updates the sheets and says in the channel who did it. A member who had been removed for inactivity is cleared by it.

2When it doesn't work

🔒 Officer

Someone outside the guild and the alliance is refused, stays flagged, and the officers are told. When Albion itself is having trouble the answer has a Retry button instead: only the officer who ran it can press it, and it registers the member once Albion answers.

3When Albion is wrong

🔒 Officer

/registration override registers someone the check refused, for when Albion's list is behind (a player who just joined, say). It still needs a character that exists, says plainly that the member was not verified, records your reason, exempts them from the audit for thirty days, and tells the other officers it happened.

4What !register says

🔒 Officer

Typing !register posts a short guide to registering. /registration guide with nothing else shows the one in use. Add your own wording (up to 1,500 characters) or a picture (png, jpg, gif or webp, up to 8 MB), or clear them to go back to the default. A file that isn't a picture, or one over the limit, is refused.

5The registration settings

🔒 Officer

/registration settings opens the Registration page of the settings menu: the roles, the nickname rules, where alerts go and the audits. On the bot's own server it also has Register-only servers, where you add another Discord server that only has /register, each with its own setup kept apart from this one.

Audit commands

Re-checking the roster

Two commands keep the roster honest. /registration audit re-checks everyone who holds the Guild or Ally role against Albion. /roster inactivity flags members with no activity for a while. Both show what they found first, and the second asks before it takes a role away.

1Re-check the roster against Albion

🔒 Officer

/registration audit with Soft refreshes nicknames and tags for everyone still verified and never takes a role away. Hard also offers to remove the role from anyone who fails the check. It can run in parts (part:1 of:4 is a quarter), and a guild roster file from the game rescues someone the game's list is behind on. The results come as a table and, when you have set a results channel, in a thread there.

2Ask people who haven't registered

🤖 The bot does this

When asking is on, the audit posts one message in the channel you chose and names only the people who can see it. The rest are listed for the officers. It never sends a private message and asks each person at most three times, a week apart.

3Find who has gone quiet

🔒 Officer

/roster inactivity looks for members with no CTA, regear or offtimer activity in the last N days, leaving out time off and newcomers. It shows who it would flag. Remove roles from everyone flagged is the only button that takes anything away, and only whoever ran the command can press it.

4What the flagged members see

🤖 The bot does this

Each flagged member is pinged with what happened and how to come back. When no one is inactive the bot says so and does nothing.

Siphon: more commands

Undoing, leaving out and adjusting

Three more /siphon commands for the cases the weekly upload doesn't cover: looking back at what was uploaded, leaving someone out of the pings, and correcting a balance by hand. They are for officers and for whoever holds the logistics role.

1Look back, and undo the newest upload

🔒 Officer

/siphon history lists the uploads so far. Only the newest can be undone, because an older one may hold lines a later upload skipped as already counted. Undoing asks first, removes only the lines that upload added, and uploading the same file again brings them back.

2Leave someone out of the pings

🔒 Officer

Someone who crafts for the guild is always behind on purpose. /siphon exempt leaves a member, or a character name from the log, out of the pings. They still show in the reports. With nobody named it lists who is left out, and remove:True puts someone back.

3Fix a balance by hand

🔒 Officer

/siphon adjust adds to or takes from a character's balance, with a reason that shows in their history. Give a member (their main character is used) or a character name, not both, and an amount that isn't zero.

Money: balances & payouts

Crediting, paying and clearing

The bot keeps each member's balance and never sends silver in the game. These are the officer's commands around it: crediting silver, looking at the guild bank, recording a payout when you have paid someone in the game, and clearing what is held for people who left. Anything that moves or clears silver shows what it will do and asks first.

1Credit silver to a balance

🔒 Officer

/balances add credits one player, or everyone who holds a role, with a note that goes on their record. It says who got what and posts a notice in the payments channel that pings only them. Give a player or a role, never both.

2The guild bank and the tax rate

🟢 Any member

/balances fund shows what the guild bank holds, what came in as tax and what went out in regears, and the tax rate that would break even. When the fund is trending down it says so and suggests a rate. With project_events it projects the fund that many events ahead at several candidate rates.

3Record that you paid someone

🔒 Officer

/pay only records a payout. Give a player to mark everything they are owed as paid, a player with an event for just that loot share, a claim for one regear, or a player with an amount to pay part of their balance. A claim can't be mixed with the other options.

4Who has received the most

🟢 Any member

/balances leaderboard ranks players by silver received or by CTA attendance, and officers can also rank by no-shows. limit says how many to show (ten by default, 25 at most) and days limits the attendance rankings to recent weeks.

5Clear what is held for people who left

🔒 Officer

/balances clearleft lists the players who are no longer in the Discord server and what is held for them: unpaid regear claims, wallet balance, unpaid loot shares. Nothing happens until Clear them, and the wallet history stays. /balances resetall is the same for everyone, and says so when there is nothing to clear.

6Reports to share

🔒 Officer 🤖 The bot does this

/export builds a fresh loot and regear report as a spreadsheet file. The weekly summary posts by itself in the channel you choose, in a private thread if you prefer, and members who are owed silver get a message once a week with a button to stop them.

CTA records

Looking up and correcting a logged CTA

After a CTA is logged, officers can look it up, correct it, change who was there and, if it was a mistake, delete it. Every change shows what it will do and asks first, and every share is worked out again from the new numbers.

1Find an event

🟢 Any member

/cta info with no number lists the recent events. With a number it shows that event's whole split: the loot, the repairs, the tax and cuts, and each player's share.

2Correct the numbers

🔒 Officer

/cta edit changes an event's loot, repair cost, tax, cuts, name or date, or takes a fight off it. It shows the new split next to the old one and waits for Apply these changes.

3Change who was there

🔒 Officer

/cta attendance adds players to an event or takes them off. Every share is recalculated, and the players are told what they now get.

4Add everyone from the signups

🔒 Officer

/cta import adds the people who signed up on the comp sheet, or who were in the fights the battleboard saw, to an event. It shows who it matched first and lets you leave someone out. With no signups on the sheet it says so.

5Delete an event

🔒 Officer

/cta delete removes an event and its attendance for good, after a preview. It refuses when a regear claim is linked to the event: the claim is an obligation of its own and shouldn't disappear with it.

Regear: ceilings & void

Price ceilings and mistakes

Two more regear jobs: setting how much a role can be regeared for, and deleting a claim that was filed wrong. Both are for officers. A price ceiling caps what a live-priced regear can pay for a role, so a Tank can't be regeared at a Healer's price.

1Set a price ceiling for a role

🔒 Officer

/regear ceiling set gives a role a General ceiling, or one for a kind of item such as Tank Weapon. A category ceiling wins over the General one for that kind of item. An amount that isn't positive is refused.

2See them and take one away

🔒 Officer

/regear ceiling list shows every ceiling, or only one role's. /regear ceiling remove takes one away and says which one it removed, or that there was none to remove. /regear ceiling copy copies all of one role's ceilings onto another.

3Delete a claim filed wrong

🔒 Officer

/regear void deletes a claim that hasn't been paid, so it can be filed again correctly. A claim already marked paid is refused, because deleting it would erase the record of silver that may have been sent: correct the balance with /balances add, or /pay with an amount, instead.

Text guide

The same story in words: how a member uses the bot, how a night runs, and officer setup.

👤 For members

The few things most members ever do.

Get set up

  • /register — prove which Albion character is yours. You get your guild role and nickname.
  • /alt — link a second character. It can sign up too, and still counts as you. If your guild pays alt shares, each of your characters that was in the battle earns you its own loot share.
  • Registering matters: it's how the bot knows which Albion character is yours, so you're found when attendance is imported and your alts and page work. Stuck? An officer can register you. Until you do, the bot reminds you now and then (at most once a day) when you sign up or use a command.

Sign up for a CTA

  • On the signup post, pick your role from the Pick your role menu. Leave gives it back and Withdraw takes you off everything. Prefer typing? Type a role's number in the thread, e.g. 5 (-5 gives it back).
  • Might come if you can? Press Tentative (or type t): you're never counted as a no-show, and you get pinged when a role opens, which you claim from the menu or by typing its number. Press it again (or type -t) to leave.
  • Taking whatever's left? Press Fill: anything, or Fill: choose roles to pick the kinds you'd take (or type fill for anything), then make sure to claim a role for attendance and loot split; your caller may place you on an open one, and you're pinged at the start if one is still open. In a separate bomb squad that shares the loot split? Press Bomb (or type bomb). Press the button again (or type -bomb, -fill) to leave.
  • Signing up on an alt? After you pick a role, a private menu lets you choose which character goes on it. Or type 5 AltName.

Check your own numbers

  • Your guild may have a member home: a pinned message with a button each for your page, your balance, filing a regear, a price check, registering, adding an alt, the open CTAs and help. A button does exactly what the command does, and only you see the answer. Prefer typing? The commands below do the same.
  • /me — your attendance, streak, sign-ups, wallet and, if your guild tracks it, your Siphoned Energy balance (what you put in minus what you took out). Only you can see it. /me owed_dms:Off stops the weekly “you're owed silver” message.
  • /balances history — your wallet. /balance — what you're owed. /balances give — give some of your wallet to another player.
  • /cta info — how a CTA's loot was split. /balances leaderboard — the top players.
  • /route — type where you are and where you want to go; I show the shortest way between them on a map, and buttons swap the ends or avoid red or black zones. Only you see it.
  • /leaderboard — the top players for kills, K/D, (K+A)/D and most deaths over 7 days, 30 days or all time, counted from your guild's battles, ten to a page, with your own place under the table. Find me and Find a name jump to a page. Only you see it. Your guild has to have it switched on.
  • /price — what any item (gear, food, potions, resources...) costs in every city.
  • /mastery show — your level on each weapon and battlemount, from how often you have played it in the CTAs and offtimers. Open its tabs to see weapons or mounts, or search by name.
  • /builds show — the gear for your role: each piece with picture, tier and amount, and equal choices. Only you see it; Send me this in DMs keeps a copy.

If you died

  • Press File a regear on your guild's regear panel (or File a regear for this battle under a battle post). Pick your character, and the death if you have several. A thread opens for you and the officers with the killboard details. If the death isn't on the killboard yet it is checked again after 24 hours and then daily for a week, and you're pinged when it turns up. After a week, post a screenshot in the thread. You need to be registered first.

Choose what you get pinged for

  • Your guild may have a roles panel: a message with numbered emojis next to roles. Click an emoji to get that role (and its pings), click it again to drop it.

🎙️ Running a CTA

For officers, and anyone with the starter role (the callers). A typical night, in order.

Before it starts

  • /cta start — pick the composition tab. Add start_time:19:00 (UTC) for a reminder and a server event.
  • Add format:Roles only for just the number and the role (the full table is the default). Officers set the usual one in the settings menu.
  • The start form's Roster button adds a live roster under the post.
  • Members pick their role from the menu in the thread (or type its number). You can type 14 @member to sign someone up and -14 @member to free them.
  • /cta claimfor — take a role over, or free one, when the shortcut above won't do.
  • People on the fill list say which kinds of role they'd take. When most roles are gone, press Place fills at the end of the thread: I suggest who takes which open role, you change any row, and the Place button gives them all their roles at once (they're pinged).
  • Wrong title or time? /signup-edit inside the thread: title:, start_time:20:00 (or none), note:Meet at the bank or board: (roster look). The post, thread, reminder and server event follow; nobody is pinged.
  • The 📋 line on the signup post counts the fill and bomb lists live. The reminders (by default 1 hour, 30 and 15 minutes before, and at the start) ping the same role as the post, in the channel, with a link to the thread; officers can change the times, who is pinged and where. Bomb squads are counted, not pinged.
  • /offtimer start — the same for side content.
  • /disarray — how many players a Disarray level takes. Type players: for your group's level, add enemy: to see who is held back and by how much, and mounts: (like 4 chariot, 2 rhino) for battle mounts, which add levels above 15 points. With nothing typed it shows every level.

After it ends

  • /cta log — enter the loot and repair cost (officers). Add preview:True first to see the split without saving anything; Add from battles on that preview puts everyone from the battleboard fights into it, and Read screenshots reads the bank tab's Est. Market Value, the castle silver bags and the party list from pictures posted in the channel (nothing is used until you pick it).
  • /cta import — pull in who came, from the sheet or battleboard fights. Leave battles empty and tick every fight of the timer from a list (each fight shows how many of your guild's players were in it, so other content is easy to skip), or paste links for fights the list doesn't show yet. Also add the signups (or source:Both) offers everyone who signed up or fought, so nobody is missed; you can skip a group or leave people out. You see a preview first. With alt shares on, a member gets one loot share for each of their registered characters in the fights (shown as ×2 in the preview).
  • Albion slow to list a fight? Press Remind me later in the picker (30 minutes to 24 hours, or a time you type) and I ping you and check again. /cta battlewatch does the same for a UTC time range and a minimum player count.
  • /lootcheck — give it the Loot Logger's export and the guild chest log to see loot that never reached the chest, listed guild first, then alliance, then everyone else. It also checks the killboard, so loot someone died carrying shows as lost on death. Open a loot thread gives a card per player with Retry deathlog search (the killboard can be late), Check a newer chest log and Resolved. Officers and the logistics role only; only they see the answer.
  • Your guild may let me finish the split by itself: you log it once, I add who was there from the battleboards, credit every share and ping each person twice. Your buttons are on a status message in the thread (🤖 By itself).
  • /cta close event_id:12 — run it inside the thread: it closes sign-ups, finds who didn't show and posts the recap.
  • /regear claim or /regear kit — pay back anyone who died.
  • /pay — pay in game, then record it: player: for all they're due, event_id: for a CTA, or Mark shares paid on its card.

🔒 Officers: setting up and keeping it running

For officers (the officer role, or anyone with Manage Server).

First time

  • /help with the First-time setup topic — a checklist that ticks itself from your real settings and changes them with buttons. Its 🚀 Quick start button fills in the basics for a new guild once you confirm a preview.
  • Much of the bot only works for registered members. Get everyone to /register; you can register anyone yourself with /registration other.
  • /welcome — see the greeting new people get. Turn it on and write your own wording in the settings menu, which can also post a note after each bot update.
  • /settings panel — post the settings menu (see "Tune it"), then open Officers & roles to choose who counts as an officer, who the callers are, and the logistics role that handles loot logs.
  • Settings menu › Logs & reports › Loot thread reminders — pings the logistics role every few days while a loot thread still has loot unresolved.
  • Settings menu › CTAs & offtimers for your Google Sheet and its composition tabs (the CTA sheet tabs and Offtimer sheet tabs buttons) and the builds tab: /builds post puts a comp's builds in front of members, /builds send DMs one.
  • /registration settings — opens the Registration page of the settings menu: the roles /register hands out, nicknames, alerts, the daily reminder and the screenshot backup. Audits have their own page. Servers that only need registration are added with its Register-only servers button. Loot & payouts › One loot share per character pays for members' alts.

Tune it

  • /settings panel — post the settings menu in an officers-only channel: one permanent message with a button for each part of the bot. This is the one place settings are changed. Click a button, pick a setting, click its choice; every change saves at once. It covers roles, loot, regear, CTAs, registration, reports, battles, the welcome message and prices.
  • /regear ceiling set — the most each role can be regeared.
  • /regear panel — let members file their own regear with a button: choose the channel, private or public threads and the regear officer roles (they approve and mark paid like officers). Each request is a thread with the death, attendance, history and wallet; Approve at guild rate files it in one click, Approve & mark paid records a payment you already sent (the bot never sends silver).
  • /officer — the jobs you do most as buttons: Start a CTA, Log a CTA, Member tools (pay, add silver, register, time off), Pay all approved, Battle report, inbox, settings and Member home (the members' buttons). Post it with channel:, or right-click a member > Apps > Officer tools.
  • /inbox — one private page with everything waiting on an officer: approved regears and loot shares to pay, requests to review, loot threads with players still owing, the Siphoned Energy upload. Mark approved regears as paid… records a batch you have already sent.
  • /digest — preview the weekly officer summary. Switch it on, and the optional DMs to members owed silver, in the settings menu.
  • /siphon upload — every couple of weeks, copy the guild's Siphoned Energy log out of the game into a .txt file and upload it. You see who has taken more than they put in and can ping them after a preview. The reminder channel is in the settings menu.
  • /reactionroles create — post a panel where members click an emoji to give themselves a role, for content pings. Powerful roles, and the officer and starter roles, are refused.

Keep it healthy

  • /registration audit — re-check everyone's guild or alliance status.
  • /roster inactivity — find members who've gone quiet.
  • /server-status — the bot's health and its last nightly backup.
  • /help with the Help board topic — post this guide in a channel; it updates itself after every bot update.
  • /help with the Guide web page topic — the whole guide as one page for people outside the server: a link that updates itself, if one is set up, and a file to forward.

🤖 What the bot does by itself

Once the settings are done, most of a guild's routine runs without anyone. What runs by itself, and the few things that still wait for an officer.

Always, in the background

  • Signup threads run themselves. Members claim a role from the menu; I keep the roster, the tentative, fill and bomb lists, the start-time reminders, the server event, no-show tracking and the recap.
  • The whole timer is collected. I watch Albion's battle list for the entire timer, keep one battleboard post up to date and keep looking for fights Albion lists late (up to three days).
  • Registration. A member who runs /register gets their roles and nickname straight away. If the nightly check is on, I also find who left, tidy nicknames and tags, and register members whose Discord name is their character's name.
  • Finding deaths. A regear request finds its death on the killboard and keeps checking until it appears. After a loot split I check for loot that never reached the chest.
  • Reports and posts. The weekly officer summary, fame tracking, the objectives board, Siphoned Energy reminders, the welcome message and nightly backups, each switched on in the settings menu.
  • Watching my own logs. Every day I check that each log and post goes to a channel the right people can see, and tell the officers once when one doesn't.

After a CTA, when the guild chose “the bot finishes it by itself”

  • You log the split once (/cta log, or Log this CTA in the signup thread). Everything after that is mine.
  • I add who was there. I read the battleboards of that timer and put everybody in the CTA's fights on the split. Anyone who isn't registered is registered by matching their Discord name to their character.
  • Other content is left out. Three people ratting a different fight at the same time are not on the CTA's split. A fight whose people are also in the CTA's fights counts, even a small one, because you only appear on a battleboard when you die or your party gets a kill. A fight I can't place is listed in the thread and, if it is worth a look, I ask an officer once.
  • Nobody is pinged early. I wait until the timer is over and no new battleboard has turned up for 6 hours (a setting). Albion can list a fight hours late.
  • Ping 1: every share is credited to the member's balance and each person is told once, with their share.
  • A late fight credits the people it adds right away and pings only them.
  • Ping 2: when the loot thread is finished (and every question about a fight is answered), I tell everybody whose total grew what was added and their combined total for the CTA. Two pings for each person, never more.
  • Your buttons are on a status message in the CTA's thread: Send pings now, Hold pings and Release the hold, Include a fight, Different timer, Undo the credits and Switch to manual. If something stops me from finishing within a day of the timer, I hand it to you and ping nobody.

What still needs a person

  • Starting a CTA, logging it once, and closing the signup (/cta start, /cta log, /cta close).
  • Approving regears and anything that takes a role away. I show what I would change and ask first.
  • Members whose Discord name isn't their character's name: they run /register, or an officer registers them.
  • Choosing how it all works: the settings menu (/settings panel) is the one place, and the setup checklist in /help ticks itself from your real settings.

Explanation & breakdown

Every command, area by area: what it does, who may use it and what to type.

Start here

The few commands to know first.

🟢 /help [topic] [channel]
This guide: pages for members, callers and officers, every command, a setup checklist and a help board. topic:Guide web page gives a link and a file to share outside the server.

🟡 /me [player] [owed_dms]
Your personal page: characters, attendance and streak, sign-up record, wallet, signups you're in. Officers can open anyone's. owed_dms:Off stops the weekly "you're owed silver" message.

🔒 /officer [channel]
Officer tools as buttons: log a CTA or offtimer, pay or register a member, watch for battles, open your inbox and settings. Post them with channel:. Right-click a member > Apps > Officer tools.

🟢 /settings show
See every setting at a glance.

🔒 /settings panel [channel]
Post the settings menu: a permanent message in an officers-only channel with a button for each part of the bot. It is the one place settings are changed, and everything saves as officers click.

🔒 /settings cleansheet [sheet]
Start a new guild from a copy of your sheet: paste the copy's address and the bot empties its roster, registrations and fame tabs. Your live sheet is never touched.

🟢 /bot-version
Which build is running, and whether the nightly audit is scheduled.

Registration

Members prove which Albion character is theirs and get their Discord roles.

🟢 /register [character_name] [screenshot]
Verify your Albion character and get your guild / alliance role. Everyone starts here.

🔒 /registration other <player> <character_name>
Register someone else on their behalf, so a member who is stuck never blocks you.

🟡 /alt <action> [character_name] [player]
Link your other Albion characters, so they can sign up for CTAs and still count as you (and earn their own loot share, if the guild pays alt shares). Officers can manage anyone's.

🔒 /registration check <player> [live_check]
Everything on record for one person: character, alts, affiliation, when they registered.

🔒 /registration override <player> <character_name> <membership_type> [notes] [exempt_days]
Register someone by hand when the Albion API gets it wrong.

🔒 /registration guide [image] [text] [clear] [guild_id]
Set the picture and wording shown when someone types !register.

🔒 /welcome
See the greeting new people get when they join the Discord (where to apply, how to register) next to its settings, which live in the settings menu.

🔒 /registration settings
Open the registration settings here: guild and ally roles, nicknames, alerts and reminders; the audits have their own page. On the bot's own server it also sets up the register-only servers.

🟡 /settings striproles <action> [role]
Extra roles /registration audit takes away from people who are no longer eligible. Anyone can list; officers add or remove.

CTA signups

Numbered signup threads for a Call to Arms, built from a composition tab in your sheet.

🎟️ /cta start <tab> [title] [ping_role] [channel] [+2 more]
Post a CTA ping and open a numbered signup thread. Add a start time (UTC) for reminders and a server event. format: shows roles only, or roles and builds.

🎟️ /cta close [event_id]
Stop new claims in a CTA thread (run it inside the thread). With event_id: also lists no-shows and posts a recap.

🎟️ /cta claimfor <action> <claim_number> [member]
Claim a role for someone else, or release one (run it inside the thread).

🎟️ /signup-edit [title] [start_time] [note] [board]
Fix a CTA or offtimer post after it's out: change the title or start time (UTC), add a note line, or change the roster look. Run it inside the thread.

🔒 /cta starter-role [role] [clear]
Choose which role may run /cta start on this server.

🟢 /disarray [players] [level] [mounts] [+3 more]
Disarray calculator: the players a level takes, a group's level (with battle mounts) and who is held back against an enemy group. Only you see it unless share:True.

🟢 /route <start> <end>
The shortest way from one zone to another, drawn on a map of the Royal Continent and the Outlands. Only you see it; buttons swap the ends or avoid red or black zones.

🟢 /mastery show [player]
Your mastery: how much you have played each weapon and battlemount, as a level in eight tiers, with what is almost there and a name search. Add player: to look at someone else. Only you see it.

🔒 /mastery add <player> <item> <plays> [note]
Add plays to a player's mastery for a weapon or battlemount by hand (a minus takes some off), for a play the signups don't show.

Builds

The gear to bring for each role, kept in a tab of your sheet and made here in Discord.

🟢 /builds show [build]
The gear to bring for a role: each piece with its picture, tier and amount, and any equal choices. Leave build: empty to pick from a list. Only you see it.

🔒 /builds post <comp> [channel]
Post a comp (a CTA tab) with the build each role brings and a menu members use to open one, in the builds channel.

🔒 /builds send <member> <build>
Send a build to a member's DMs.

🎟️ /builds create [name] [copy]
Make a build here: a private editor with the gear picture, item search, tier and enchantment, up to three choices per slot and skills and passives. Saved to the builds tab of your sheet.

🎟️ /builds edit <build>
Change a build that is on the sheet in the same editor. Only the cells that differ are written.

🎟️ /builds delete <build>
Remove a build from the sheet after asking (its cells are emptied, your formatting stays).

🔒 /builds setup
Choose between the original table pictures and builds (both shown side by side), make the BUILDS tab, and draft builds from your comp tabs. Nothing is written until you press Write.

🔒 /builds status
Where builds stand: the tab, each comp's roles with and without a build, and buttons to sync from comps, make a build or give a role its build.

CTA loot & attendance

Log an event's loot, record who came, and split it. Only on the bot's own server and full-bot servers.

🔒 /cta log [name] [loot] [repair_cost] [+8 more]
Log a Call to Arms: loot, repair and attendees. No options gives a form. On the preview, Add from battles and Read screenshots fill things in. Nothing is saved until Log it. Dates are UTC.

🔒 /cta attendance <action> <event_id> <players>
Add players to an event's attendance, or remove them.

🎟️ /lootcheck <loot_log> <chest_log> [loot_log_2] [loot_log_3] [loot_log_4] [+9 more]
Who picked up loot that never reached the chest (guild, then alliance, then outsiders). Loot someone died carrying counts as lost on death. Opens a loot thread. Officers and logistics role.

🔒 /cta import <event_id> [comp_sheet_gid] [source] [battles]
Add attendees from the signup sheet and/or battleboard fights. Both adds everyone on either list, so nobody is missed. Tick the fights from a list or be reminded later; preview, then confirm.

🔒 /cta battlewatch
Watch a UTC time range with a minimum player count (and how many of yours) and get pinged when fights in it show up. See and cancel your reminders and watches.

🔒 /cta edit <event_id> [loot] [repair_cost] [tax_rate] [+7 more]
Fix anything on a logged event: loot, silver bags, repair, percentages, name, date (UTC), people, fights, late loot. On its own it opens an Edit menu. Every change is remembered.

🟢 /cta info [event_id] [limit]
One event's full loot split, who signed up but didn't show, and what was changed after it was logged. With no event_id: the recent events.

🔒 /cta delete <event_id>
Permanently delete an event and its attendance (asks first).

Siphoned Energy

Who put in more Siphoned Energy than they took out, from the game's log. Only on the bot's own server and full-bot servers.

🎟️ /siphon upload <file>
Upload the Siphoned Energy log copied from the game (a .txt). Only new lines are counted, so overlapping uploads are safe. Shows who is behind, with buttons to ping them or undo.

🎟️ /siphon report [player] [days] [post]
Everyone's balance (put in minus taken out): who is behind, who is ahead, with a spreadsheet file. Or open one player's page.

🎟️ /siphon ping [behind_by] [channel]
Name the members who are behind in a channel. You see who first and confirm before anything is sent.

🎟️ /siphon history [undo]
The uploads so far. Undo the newest one.

🔒 /siphon exempt [member] [name] [remove]
Leave someone out of the pings (the guild's crafter, say), or put them back.

🔒 /siphon adjust <amount> [member] [name] [reason]
Add to or take from someone's balance by hand, e.g. energy paid in before the first log.

Regear

Price a death from live market data (or the killboard), cap it by role, and file the claim.

🔒 /regear claim <player> <role> <item_id> [item_name] [category] [event_id] [+3 more]
File a regear claim at the cheapest market price for the item's quality (any city but Caerleon, equal-power tiers), capped by role. Optional EST.

🔒 /regear kit [player] [character] [role] [+2 more]
Price a player's whole death from the killboard, each item at its own quality, and file their regear. Enter an EST or pick another quality if needed.

🔒 /regear panel [channel] [visibility] [ping] [post]
Set up member regear requests: the File a regear button, private or public threads, who reviews them. Members file, the bot finds the death and rechecks daily; you approve in one click.

🔒 /regear custom <player> <amount> <reason> [event_id] [notes]
File a claim for an amount you type -- no lookup, no cap.

🟢 /regear info [claim_id] [status] [limit]
One claim in full. With no claim_id: a list of claims.

🔒 /regear void <claim_id>
Delete an unpaid claim so it can be refiled correctly.

🔒 /regear ceiling set <role> <amount> [category]
Set the most silver a role can be regeared (optionally per item category).

🔒 /regear ceiling remove <role> [category]
Remove a role's ceiling.

🔒 /regear ceiling copy <from_role> <to_role>
Copy every ceiling from one role to another.

🟢 /regear ceiling list [role]
Show the role ceilings.

🟢 /price <item> [quality]
What any item costs right now in every city (gear, food, potions, mounts, resources...), from the Albion Online Data Project.

Payouts & balances

Pay people, and track the wallet balance, the guild bank and the reports.

🔒 /inbox
Everything waiting on an officer on one private page: payouts to send (with a button to mark approved regears paid), regear requests to review, loot threads, the Siphoned Energy upload.

🔒 /pay [player] [event_id] [claim_id] [+2 more]
Record a payout: all a player is owed (player), a whole event (event_id), one claim (claim_id) or part of a wallet (player + amount). The member menu's Pay what's owed does the first.

🟢 /balances history [player] [everyone] [transactions] [limit]
A player's wallet by source (what they were paid, and where the wallet came from). Also their transactions, or everyone with a balance.

🟢 /balance [player]
What the guild owes you, or the player you pick: pending loot and regear plus the wallet. !bal does the same in chat (!bal @member for someone else).

🟢 /balances fund [project_events]
The guild bank / regear fund's health, or a projection at other tax rates.

🟢 /balances give <player> <amount> [note]
Give some of your own wallet balance to another player. It asks first, and both of you see it on the records.

🟡 /balances leaderboard [limit] [by] [days]
Top players by silver received or CTA attendance. Officers can also rank no-shows.

🔒 /digest
Preview this week's officer summary (CTAs, offtimers, what's owed, new members) and see when it posts. The summary and the optional owed-silver DMs are set up in the settings menu.

🔒 /balances add <amount> [player] [role] [notes]
Credit silver to one player's wallet, or to everyone holding a role.

🔒 /balances resetall
Clear everyone's balances: delete unpaid regears and zero every wallet.

🔒 /balances clearleft
Clear what is held for players who left the Discord (not just the guild): lists them, then asks first.

🔒 /export
Generate a fresh loot / regear report (.xlsx).

Offtimers

Content outside the main CTA, kept separate: its own signups, loot split and wallet credit.

🎟️ /offtimer start <tab> [title] [ping_role] [channel] [+3 more]
Post an offtimer ping and open a numbered signup thread. Add a start time (UTC) and everyone sees it in their own timezone.

🎟️ /offtimer close

🔒 /offtimer unattend <event_id> <players>
Remove players and recalculate the split (asks first).

🔒 /offtimer delete <event_id>

🟢 /offtimer info [event_id] [limit]
One offtimer event's breakdown. With no event_id: the recent ones.

Audits & activity

People & roles

The roster, recruiting, giveaways, bulk role changes and self-assign role panels.

🔒 /roster add <player> [role]

🔒 /reactionroles edit <panel> <action> [role] [emoji]
Add or remove a role on a panel, switch "pick one only" mode, or delete the panel.

🔒 /reactionroles list
The role panels in this server, with a link to each.

Fame, battleboard & objectives

Optional automatic features: weekly fame progress, battle summaries and the open-world objectives board, posted to a channel.

🔒 /fame check [player] [character_name]
Look up one player's current fame -- to confirm tracking works.

🔒 /fame report [new_snapshot]
Show the latest fame report, or take a fresh snapshot first.

🔒 /fame audit
Re-verify everyone's guild / alliance status for tracking.

🔒 /fame exclude <players> [until] [notes]
Leave someone out of fame tracking without un-registering them.

🔒 /fame untrack <players>
Stop tracking someone who has left.

🔒 /battleboard config [entity_type] [name] [channel] [+8 more]
Set up or change automatic battleboard posting.

🟢 /battleboard status
Show the current battleboard setup.

🔒 /battleboard test
Run one check now and show the most recent battle.

🔒 /battleboard report [battles] [public]
Several fights in one report: alliance and guild table cards, Remove Rats, the kill timeline and momentum charts, and a comparison of every guild.

🔒 /battleboard leftearly
See who left CTA timers early and how often, and excuse a time that should not count.

🔒 /battleboard stop
Turn off automatic battleboard posting.

🟢 /leaderboard
The top players over 7 days, 30 days or all time (kills, K/D, (K+A)/D, most deaths), ten to a page, with your own place and buttons to find yourself or a name. Only you see it; a button posts a copy.

🟢 /objectives report
Report an open-world objective (its kind, zone and when it opens) so it goes on the objectives board.

🔒 /objectives status
Is the objectives board working? Its channels, the scanner and when it last reported.

🔒 /objectives remove
Take an objective off the board, for example a wrong report.

🔒 /objectives scannerlink
Make the webhook link the scanner program posts through. It is shown once, and only to you.

Bot health

Run on the bot's own server only: check how the bot is doing. (Register-only servers are set up in the settings menu, under Registration.)

🔒 /server-status [backup_now]
The bot's health: servers it runs, its nightly jobs and the last backup. Can run a backup now.
